Others said: It is the soul when it is dragged forth.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The soul when it is drowned in the chest."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by "those who drag forth violently", and He did not specify one dragging over another. Thus every dragging forth violently falls within His oath, whether it is angels, death, stars, bows, or other things. The meaning is: "And by those who drag forth with violence, as one who draws on a bow drags."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾

The people of interpretation also differed concerning them: what are they, and what is it that is released? Some of them said: They are the angels, who release the soul of the believer and take it, as a camel's hobble (iqal) is loosened when it is untied from it.

Mention of those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The angels."

al-Farra' used to say: What I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: "anshatat" (she released), as if released from a hobble (iqal), and "rabtuha" (I tied it) means "nashatuha" (I released it); and the one who ties is "al-rabit", and the one who releases is "al-nashit". He said: When you tie the rope on the camel's foot you have "nashatah" (you bound it), and you are "nashit"; and when you untie it you have "anshatah" (you released it).

Others said: ﴿al-nashitat nashta﴾ is death, which releases the soul of a human being.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "Death."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "When its soul is released."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "He releases it when it is released from the two feet."

Others said: They are the stars that are released from horizon to horizon.
Mention of those who said this:
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, his saying: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The stars."
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "They are the stars."

Others said: They are the nooses (al-awhaq).
[[The scholars discussed the refutation of what Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) held, that "al-hamd" and "al-shukr" have one meaning and that one may be placed in the position of the other; this is also what al-Mubarrad held. See al-Qurtubi 1:116 and Ibn Kathir 1:42. The citation from al-Qurtubi was mistaken, as he thought he had cited it in support of al-Tabari's view, which is an error. What al-Tabari said is stronger in argument and more ancient in Arabic than those who refuted him. His saying "a verbal noun of ashkara", and his saying "that it proceeds from al-hamd", means by it the absolute object (al-maf'ul al-mutlaq). See what has passed: 117, note 1.]]
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The nooses."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by "those who gently release", which are those that release from one place to another, going to it. God did not specify anything among them over anything else; rather the oath includes all those who release, and the angels release from place to place, and likewise death, and likewise the stars, the nooses, and also the wild cattle release, as al-Tirimmah said:

"Has there been in the allied horses, of those I knew,
other than the wild cattle of the nawashit (the wild herds), a fright?"

By the nawashit he means the wild cattle, because they release from town to town, as Ru'bah ibn al-Ajjaj said:

"Every fenced-in noose-held one released him..."

And worries release their companion, as Himan ibn Qahafah said:

"My worries have become those that release the places,
Syria with me at one time and Wasit at another."

[[Found in the interpretation of the verse of Surat al-Mu'minun: 87 (18:27 Bulaq). He attributed the two verses to some of the Banu 'Amir; likewise in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:170. Both are in al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin 3:184, attributed to al-Wuzari, whom I did not identify, and there is variation in the transmission. al-Rams: the grave with earth heaped over it. He says: it has become a grave that is visited or lamented over. al-Jahiz transmitted: "sa-asir mayyitan" (I shall become dead), which is nothing. al-Nawa'ij is the plural of na'ijah: swift camels, which move swiftly in their travel, i.e. they went in every direction from their vigour. In al-Bayan and al-Farra's Ma'ani it is "al-nawaj", which is nothing.]]

So every released thing is included in what He swore by, unless there is a proof that must be accepted establishing that the intended object of the oath is some and not others.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And those who glide swiftly."

The people of interpretation differed concerning those by which He swore, may His praise be exalted, from among the swimmers (al-sabihat). Some of them said: They are death, gliding into the soul of the son of Adam.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "Death"; thus I found it in my book.
• And Ibn Humayd has also narrated it to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "The angels." Thus I found this also in my book. If what we have mentioned from Ibn Humayd is sound, then Mujahid held that the descent of the angels from heaven is gliding (sabbahah), as one says of a noble horse: "innahu la-sabih" (indeed he is gliding) when it passes swiftly.

Others said: They are the stars that glide in their orbit.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "They are the stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: They are the ships.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "The ships."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by those who glide swiftly among His creation, and He did not specify some of that over others. Thus every swimmer (sabih) is included, as we described before concerning the released ones [[It comes in the interpretation of verses of Surat al-Baqarah: 7, Surat Al 'Imran: 49, Surat al-Ma'idah: 53, Surat al-An'am: 99, Surat al-Anfal: 14, Surat Yunus: 71, and Surat al-Rahman: 22. It is a verse cited as evidence in every book.]].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning them. Some of them said: They are the angels.
Mention of those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "The angels."
• Abu Kurayb also narrated this hadith to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "Death."

Others said: Rather, they are the swift horses.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "The horses."

Others said: Rather, they are the stars, one of which overtakes another in its course.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "They are the stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Our view on these is like our view on the other preceding words.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾

He says: "Then the angels who arrange what they are commanded of God's command." And thus the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾, he said: "They are the angels."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: On the day the earth and the mountains quake at the first blast ﴿followed by the following one﴾, the other coming after it, which is the second blast, that followed the first for the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

Mention of those who said this:
• Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he says: "The first blast."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Followed by the following one﴾

He says: "The second blast."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he says: "The last follows the first; the quaking one is the first blast and the following one is the last blast."
• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are the two blasts: the first kills the living, and the second brings the dead to life." Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾.
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are two cries: the first causes everything to die by God's permission, and the other brings everything to life by God's permission. The Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'Between them is forty.' His companions said: 'By God, he added nothing to that for us.' And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'In those forty there will be sent a rain called al-Hayah (Life), until the earth becomes good and stirs, and the bodies of people sprout like herbs; then the second is blown, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.'"
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ said, and he mentioned the Trumpet (al-sur). Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn." He said: "What is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of standing up. The people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. God will command it to be prolonged and extended, and it will not slacken; and it is the one that says: 'These only await one cry, with no pause (fawaq).' Then God will set the mountains in motion, and they will become a mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people with a violent shaking. It is the one of which He says: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one, hearts that Day will be trembling﴾."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ recited: "On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one," and said: "The quaking one has come, followed by the following one; death has come with what is in it."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾: the first blast; ﴿followed by the following one﴾: the other blast.

Others said regarding that:
• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he said: "The earth and the mountains quake, and it is the earthquake." And His saying: ﴿the following one﴾, he said: "It is His saying: ﴿When the heaven is split open﴾ ﴿and it is crushed with one crushing﴾."

Others said: The earth quakes, and the following one is the Hour.
Mention of those who said this:
• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, "the earth"; and concerning His saying: ﴿followed by the following one﴾, he said: "The following one is the Hour."

The people of Arabic grammar differed concerning the place of the response (jawab) to His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His saying ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾ is an oath, and God knows best, upon ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾. And if you wish, you may make it upon ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾ and ﴿hearts that Day will be trembling﴾; and it is as God said, and He willed that it be in all of this, and in all matters. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The response to the oath in "al-nazi'at" is omitted, because its meaning is known to the listeners; as if it were made apparent, it would be: "You will indeed be resurrected and called to account." He said: This is shown by His saying: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Do you not see that it is like the response to His saying: ﴿You will indeed be resurrected﴾, when He said: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Another of them said something similar to this, except that he said: It is not permitted to omit the lam in the response to an oath, because if it is omitted its place is not known, since it precedes every speech.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that the response to the oath in this place is something that is dispensed with because the meaning of the speech indicates it, so its mention is omitted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the hearts of His creatures that Day will be fearful of the great terror that descends.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿trembling﴾: fearful.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful, quaking from what they witnessed that Day.

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: the trembling (wajifa) is the fearful.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾
He means: the eyes of their owners will be humbled, overcome by sorrow and grief, from the fear and dread that has come upon them from the great terror of that Day.
As:
⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: downcast from the humiliation that has come upon them.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: humbled.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 1–9 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently, and by those who gently release, and by those who glide swiftly, and by those who race ahead, and by those who arrange affairs, on the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one, hearts that Day will be trembling, their eyes humbled﴾.

Our Lord, may His majesty be exalted, swore by "al-nazi'at" (those who drag forth). The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning them: what are they, and what do they drag forth? Some of them said: They are the angels who drag forth the souls of the children of Adam, and what is dragged forth is the souls of human beings.

Mention of those who said this:
• Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah, regarding ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The angels."
• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, that he used to say concerning "al-nazi'at": they are the angels.
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "al-nazi'at", he said: "When its soul is dragged forth."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The souls are dragged forth."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "Their spirits were dragged forth, then they were drowned, then they were cast into the Fire."

Others said: Rather, it is death that drags forth souls.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "Death."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: They are the stars that are dragged from horizon to horizon.
• al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, that he heard al-Hasan concerning ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The stars."

Others said: They are the bows that drag the arrow.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The bows" (al-qisiyy).

Others said: It is the soul when it is dragged forth.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The soul when it is drowned in the chest."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by "those who drag forth violently", and He did not specify one dragging over another. Thus every dragging forth violently falls within His oath, whether it is angels, death, stars, bows, or other things. The meaning is: "And by those who drag forth with violence, as one who draws on a bow drags."

Both are in al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin 3:184, attributed to al-Wuzari, whom I did not identify, and there is variation in the transmission. al-Rams: the grave with earth heaped over it. He says: it has become a grave that is visited or lamented over. al-Jahiz transmitted: "sa-asir mayyitan" (I shall become dead), which is nothing. al-Nawa'ij is the plural of na'ijah: swift camels, which move swiftly in their travel, i.e. they went in every direction from their vigour. In al-Bayan and al-Farra's Ma'ani it is "al-nawaj", which is nothing.]]

So every released thing is included in what He swore by, unless there is a proof that must be accepted establishing that the intended object of the oath is some and not others.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And those who glide swiftly."

The people of interpretation differed concerning those by which He swore, may His praise be exalted, from among the swimmers (al-sabihat). Some of them said: They are death, gliding into the soul of the son of Adam.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "Death"; thus I found it in my book.
• And Ibn Humayd has also narrated it to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "The angels." Thus I found this also in my book. If what we have mentioned from Ibn Humayd is sound, then Mujahid held that the descent of the angels from heaven is gliding (sabbahah), as one says of a noble horse: "innahu la-sabih" (indeed he is gliding) when it passes swiftly.

Others said: They are the stars that glide in their orbit.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "They are the stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: They are the ships.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who glide swiftly﴾, he said: "The ships."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by those who glide swiftly among His creation, and He did not specify some of that over others. Thus every swimmer (sabih) is included, as we described before concerning the released ones [[It comes in the interpretation of verses of Surat al-Baqarah: 7, Surat Al 'Imran: 49, Surat al-Ma'idah: 53, Surat al-An'am: 99, Surat al-Anfal: 14, Surat Yunus: 71, and Surat al-Rahman: 22. It is a verse cited as evidence in every book.]].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning them. Some of them said: They are the angels.
Mention of those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "The angels."
• Abu Kurayb also narrated this hadith to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "Death."

Others said: Rather, they are the swift horses.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "The horses."

Others said: Rather, they are the stars, one of which overtakes another in its course.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who race ahead, racing﴾, he said: "They are the stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Our view on these is like our view on the other preceding words.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾

He says: "Then the angels who arrange what they are commanded of God's command." And thus the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾, he said: "They are the angels."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: On the day the earth and the mountains quake at the first blast ﴿followed by the following one﴾, the other coming after it, which is the second blast, that followed the first for the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

Mention of those who said this:
• Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he says: "The first blast."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Followed by the following one﴾

He says: "The second blast."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he says: "The last follows the first; the quaking one is the first blast and the following one is the last blast."
• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are the two blasts: the first kills the living, and the second brings the dead to life." Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾.
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are two cries: the first causes everything to die by God's permission, and the other brings everything to life by God's permission. The Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'Between them is forty.' His companions said: 'By God, he added nothing to that for us.' And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'In those forty there will be sent a rain called al-Hayah (Life), until the earth becomes good and stirs, and the bodies of people sprout like herbs; then the second is blown, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.'"
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ said, and he mentioned the Trumpet (al-sur). Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn." He said: "What is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of standing up. The people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. God will command it to be prolonged and extended, and it will not slacken; and it is the one that says: 'These only await one cry, with no pause (fawaq).' Then God will set the mountains in motion, and they will become a mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people with a violent shaking. It is the one of which He says: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one, hearts that Day will be trembling﴾."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ recited: "On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one," and said: "The quaking one has come, followed by the following one; death has come with what is in it."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾: the first blast; ﴿followed by the following one﴾: the other blast.

Others said regarding that:
• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he said: "The earth and the mountains quake, and it is the earthquake." And His saying: ﴿the following one﴾, he said: "It is His saying: ﴿When the heaven is split open﴾ ﴿and it is crushed with one crushing﴾."

Others said: The earth quakes, and the following one is the Hour.
Mention of those who said this:
• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, "the earth"; and concerning His saying: ﴿followed by the following one﴾, he said: "The following one is the Hour."

The people of Arabic grammar differed concerning the place of the response (jawab) to His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His saying ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾ is an oath, and God knows best, upon ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾. And if you wish, you may make it upon ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾ and ﴿hearts that Day will be trembling﴾; and it is as God said, and He willed that it be in all of this, and in all matters. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The response to the oath in "al-nazi'at" is omitted, because its meaning is known to the listeners; as if it were made apparent, it would be: "You will indeed be resurrected and called to account." He said: This is shown by His saying: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Do you not see that it is like the response to His saying: ﴿You will indeed be resurrected﴾, when He said: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Another of them said something similar to this, except that he said: It is not permitted to omit the lam in the response to an oath, because if it is omitted its place is not known, since it precedes every speech.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that the response to the oath in this place is something that is dispensed with because the meaning of the speech indicates it, so its mention is omitted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the hearts of His creatures that Day will be fearful of the great terror that descends.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿trembling﴾: fearful.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful, quaking from what they witnessed that Day.

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: the trembling (wajifa) is the fearful.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾
He means: the eyes of their owners will be humbled, overcome by sorrow and grief, from the fear and dread that has come upon them from the great terror of that Day.
As:
⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: downcast from the humiliation that has come upon them.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: humbled.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 1–9 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently, and by those who gently release, and by those who glide swiftly, and by those who race ahead, and by those who arrange affairs, on the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one, hearts that Day will be trembling, their eyes humbled﴾.

Our Lord, may His majesty be exalted, swore by "al-nazi'at" (those who drag forth). The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning them: what are they, and what do they drag forth? Some of them said: They are the angels who drag forth the souls of the children of Adam, and what is dragged forth is the souls of human beings.

Mention of those who said this:
• Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah, regarding ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The angels."
• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, that he used to say concerning "al-nazi'at": they are the angels.
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "al-nazi'at", he said: "When its soul is dragged forth."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The souls are dragged forth."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "Their spirits were dragged forth, then they were drowned, then they were cast into the Fire."

Others said: Rather, it is death that drags forth souls.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "Death."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: They are the stars that are dragged from horizon to horizon.
• al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Awwam narrated to us, that he heard al-Hasan concerning ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The stars."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The stars."

Others said: They are the bows that drag the arrow.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The bows" (al-qisiyy).

Others said: It is the soul when it is dragged forth.
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾, he said: "The soul when it is drowned in the chest."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, swore by "those who drag forth violently", and He did not specify one dragging over another. Thus every dragging forth violently falls within His oath, whether it is angels, death, stars, bows, or other things. The meaning is: "And by those who drag forth with violence, as one who draws on a bow drags."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾

The people of interpretation also differed concerning them: what are they, and what is it that is released? Some of them said: They are the angels, who release the soul of the believer and take it, as a camel's hobble (iqal) is loosened when it is untied from it.

Mention of those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The angels."

al-Farra' used to say: What I have heard from the Arabs is that they say: "anshatat" (she released), as if released from a hobble (iqal), and "rabtuha" (I tied it) means "nashatuha" (I released it); and the one who ties is "al-rabit", and the one who releases is "al-nashit". He said: When you tie the rope on the camel's foot you have "nashatah" (you bound it), and you are "nashit"; and when you untie it you have "anshatah" (you released it).

Others said: ﴿al-nashitat nashta﴾ is death, which releases the soul of a human being.

Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "Death."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "When its soul is released."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "He releases it when it is released from the two feet."

Others said: They are the stars that are released from horizon to horizon.
Mention of those who said this:
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, his saying: ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The stars."
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "They are the stars."

Others said: They are the nooses (al-awhaq).
[[The scholars discussed the refutation of what Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) held, that "al-hamd" and "al-shukr" have one meaning and that one may be placed in the position of the other; this is also what al-Mubarrad held. See al-Qurtubi 1:116 and Ibn Kathir 1:42. The citation from al-Qurtubi was mistaken, as he thought he had cited it in support of al-Tabari's view, which is an error. What al-Tabari said is stronger in argument and more ancient in Arabic than those who refuted him. His saying "a verbal noun of ashkara", and his saying "that it proceeds from al-hamd", means by it the absolute object (al-maf'ul al-mutlaq). See what has passed: 117, note 1.]]
Mention of those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Ata', ﴿And by those who gently release﴾, he said: "The nooses."

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, swore by "those who gently release", which are those that release from one place to another, going to it. God did not specify anything among them over anything else; rather the oath includes all those who release, and the angels release from place to place, and likewise death, and likewise the stars, the nooses, and also the wild cattle release, as al-Tirimmah said:

"Has there been in the allied horses, of those I knew,
other than the wild cattle of the nawashit (the wild herds), a fright?"

By the nawashit he means the wild cattle, because they release from town to town, as Ru'bah ibn al-Ajjaj said:

"Every fenced-in noose-held one released him..."

And worries release their companion, as Himan ibn Qahafah said:

"My worries have become those that release the places,
Syria with me at one time and Wasit at another."

[[Found in the interpretation of the verse of Surat al-Mu'minun: 87 (18:27 Bulaq). He attributed the two verses to some of the Banu 'Amir; likewise in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:170. Both are in al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin 3:184, attributed to al-Wuzari, whom I did not identify, and there is variation in the transmission. al-Rams: the grave with earth heaped over it. He says: it has become a grave that is visited or lamented over. al-Jahiz transmitted: "sa-asir mayyitan" (I shall become dead), which is nothing. al-Nawa'ij is the plural of na'ijah: swift camels, which move swiftly in their travel, i.e. they went in every direction from their vigour. In al-Bayan and al-Farra's Ma'ani it is "al-nawaj", which is nothing.]]

So every released thing is included in what He swore by, unless there is a proof that must be accepted establishing that the intended object of the oath is some and not others.

• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Our view on these is like our view on the other preceding words.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾

He says: "Then the angels who arrange what they are commanded of God's command." And thus the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said this:
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾, he said: "They are the angels."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: On the day the earth and the mountains quake at the first blast ﴿followed by the following one﴾, the other coming after it, which is the second blast, that followed the first for the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

Mention of those who said this:
• Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he says: "The first blast."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Followed by the following one﴾

He says: "The second blast."
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he says: "The last follows the first; the quaking one is the first blast and the following one is the last blast."
• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are the two blasts: the first kills the living, and the second brings the dead to life." Then al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾.
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one﴾, he said: "They are two cries: the first causes everything to die by God's permission, and the other brings everything to life by God's permission. The Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'Between them is forty.' His companions said: 'By God, he added nothing to that for us.' And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ used to say: 'In those forty there will be sent a rain called al-Hayah (Life), until the earth becomes good and stirs, and the bodies of people sprout like herbs; then the second is blown, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.'"
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ said, and he mentioned the Trumpet (al-sur). Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of God, what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn." He said: "What is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of standing up. The people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. God will command it to be prolonged and extended, and it will not slacken; and it is the one that says: 'These only await one cry, with no pause (fawaq).' Then God will set the mountains in motion, and they will become a mirage, and the earth will be shaken with its people with a violent shaking. It is the one of which He says: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one, hearts that Day will be trembling﴾."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ﴿ﷺ﴾ recited: "On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one," and said: "The quaking one has come, followed by the following one; death has come with what is in it."
• I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾: the first blast; ﴿followed by the following one﴾: the other blast.

Others said regarding that:
• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, he said: "The earth and the mountains quake, and it is the earthquake." And His saying: ﴿the following one﴾, he said: "It is His saying: ﴿When the heaven is split open﴾ ﴿and it is crushed with one crushing﴾."

Others said: The earth quakes, and the following one is the Hour.
Mention of those who said this:
• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾, "the earth"; and concerning His saying: ﴿followed by the following one﴾, he said: "The following one is the Hour."

The people of Arabic grammar differed concerning the place of the response (jawab) to His saying: ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His saying ﴿By those who drag forth violently﴾ is an oath, and God knows best, upon ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾. And if you wish, you may make it upon ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes﴾ and ﴿hearts that Day will be trembling﴾; and it is as God said, and He willed that it be in all of this, and in all matters. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The response to the oath in "al-nazi'at" is omitted, because its meaning is known to the listeners; as if it were made apparent, it would be: "You will indeed be resurrected and called to account." He said: This is shown by His saying: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Do you not see that it is like the response to His saying: ﴿You will indeed be resurrected﴾, when He said: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and crumbled dust?﴾. Another of them said something similar to this, except that he said: It is not permitted to omit the lam in the response to an oath, because if it is omitted its place is not known, since it precedes every speech.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 1–9 (part 2 of 2):

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that the response to the oath in this place is something that is dispensed with because the meaning of the speech indicates it, so its mention is omitted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the hearts of His creatures that Day will be fearful of the great terror that descends.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿trembling﴾: fearful.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿trembling﴾, he said: fearful.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: fearful, quaking from what they witnessed that Day.

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Hearts that Day will be trembling﴾, he said: the trembling (wajifa) is the fearful.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾
He means: the eyes of their owners will be humbled, overcome by sorrow and grief, from the fear and dread that has come upon them from the great terror of that Day.
As:
⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: downcast from the humiliation that has come upon them.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Their eyes will be downcast﴾, he said: humbled.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verses 10–14:

On the explanation (ta'wil, interpretation) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Shall we indeed be returned to our former state? (10) Even when we have become decayed bones?" (11) They say, "That would then be a losing return." (12) But it will be only a single blast, (13) and at once they will be upon the awakened surface.﴾ (14)

Exalted is His remembrance. He says: These deniers of the Resurrection among the polytheists of Quraysh say, when they are told, "You will be resurrected after death": "Shall we indeed be returned to our former state before death, and come back alive as we were before our destruction and before our dying?" This is from their saying, "So-and-so returned upon his hafira (trail, the way he came)," meaning he went back the way he had come. From it is the words of the poet:

"Going back along our trail, over baldness and gray hair? God forbid such folly and frivolity."[[See what has passed above at hadith no. 151.]]

Those who explain the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* ʿAlī told me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿al-ḥāfira﴾: he said, "Life."

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾: he said, "Shall we indeed be made to live after our death and be resurrected from this place of ours?"

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾ "Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿in the hāfira﴾: he said, "That is, shall we be returned as a new creation?"

* Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Abū Maʿshar, from Muḥammad ibn Qays or Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, regarding ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾: he said, "In life."

* Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾: he said, "In life."

Others said: al-Ḥāfira is the dug-up earth in which their graves were dug. They made this parallel to His words ﴿from a gushing water﴾, meaning "gushed." They said: al-ḥāfira has the sense of al-maḥfūra (the dug-up), and the meaning of the statement for them is: "Shall we indeed be returned in our graves as dead?"

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿al-ḥāfira﴾: he said, "The earth: we will be resurrected as a new creation." He said, "The resurrection."

* al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿Shall we indeed be returned in the ḥāfira?﴾: he said, "The earth; we will be resurrected as a new creation."

Others said: al-Ḥāfira is the Fire.

Those who said this:

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say concerning the words of God ﴿Shall we indeed be returned in the ḥāfira?﴾: "The ḥāfira is the Fire." He recited the words of God ﴿That would then be a losing return﴾ and said: "How many are its names! It is the Fire, it is al-Jaḥīm, it is Saqar, it is Jahannam, it is al-Hāwiya, it is al-Ḥāfira, it is Laẓā, it is al-Ḥuṭama."

* * *

As for His words ﴿Even when we have become decayed bones?﴾

The readers (qurrāʾ) differed in reciting this. The majority of readers of Medina, the Ḥijāz and Basra recited ﴿nakhira﴾, meaning "decayed." The majority of readers of Kufa recited ﴿nākhira﴾ with an alif, meaning that they are hollow, through which the winds blow when they pass through them. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language among the Kufans said: al-nākhira and al-nakhira are the same in meaning, like al-ṭāmiʿ and al-ṭamiʿ, and al-bākhil and al-bakhil. In our view, however, the more eloquent and more widely known of the two dialects is ﴿nakhira﴾, without alif, meaning "decayed." Nevertheless, the verse-endings before and after it came with an alif, so it is more pleasing to me to add the alif to it (nākhira) so that it agrees with the rest of the verse-endings. Were it not for that, the more pleasing of the two readings to me would be to omit the alif.

Those who said that ﴿nakhira﴾ means "decayed":

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding ﴿Even when we have become decayed bones?﴾: "al-nakhira: the perished, the decayed."

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿decayed bones﴾: he said, "Crumbled."

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Even when we have become bones﴾ in denial of the Resurrection, ﴿nākhira﴾: "decayed." They said: ﴿That would then be a losing return﴾. Its meaning, exalted is His praise, is the speech of these deniers of the Resurrection, who said: "That," meaning that return to life after death; "then," meaning now; "a return," meaning a coming back; "losing," meaning ruinous.

And according to what we have said, the exegetes have said likewise.

Those who said this:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿then a losing return﴾: "That is, a losing return."

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿That would then be a losing return﴾: "And what return is more losing than it? They were brought to life and then went to the Fire, so it was an evil return."

* * *

As for His words ﴿But it will be only a single blast﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: It will only be a single cry and one blast blown into the Trumpet, and that is the zajra (blast).

According to what we have said, the exegetes have said likewise.

Those who said this:

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿a single blast﴾: he said, "A cry."

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿a single blast﴾: "The zajra is the blast in the Trumpet."

* * *

As for His words ﴿and at once they will be upon the awakened surface﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then at once these deniers of the Resurrection, who marvel at God's bringing them to life after their death, in denial of that, will be upon the sāhira (awakened surface), meaning the surface of the earth. The Arabs call the desert and the face of the earth sāhira, and I think they named it so because in it the animals sleep and stay awake, so it is described by a quality of what is in it. From it is the words of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:

"And in it is the flesh of the sāhira and the sea, and what they say is established for them."[[His Dīwān, poem 15/32. The lord of Kinda is Ḥujr, father of Imru' al-Qays. The lord of Maʿadd: Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr, as the commentator of his Dīwān says, though I am doubtful about it, for Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr was killed at al-Habāʾa. Labīd mentions Khabt and ʿAraʿar, which are two other places.]]

From it is also the words of Akhū Nahm on the day of Dhū Qār, to his horse:

"Advance, Miḥāj, for these are the bracelets (of the battle); and let no single unknown man terrify you. For your end is the dust of the sāhira, then you will return after it to the trail, after you were decayed bones."[[His Dīwān: 89; al-Mukhaṣṣaṣ 7:154. al-Ṭarīf and al-Ṭārif: newly acquired wealth, as opposed to al-Talīd and al-Tālid, which is the old wealth you were born with.]]

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm told me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "On the earth." He said: He then mentioned a poem composed by Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, and said:

"With us is the game of the sea and the game of the sāhira."[[His Dīwān: 25. salaʾa al-samn yaslauhu: he cooked it and treated it, melting its cream. al-salāʾ, with a kasra on the sīn: ghee. ḥaqana al-laban fi al-waṭb, and al-māʾ fi al-siqāʾ: he held it in it and filled it. rabba naḥā al-samn yarubbuhu: he greased it with rubb, which is the syrup of every fruit; they used to grease the skin of the waterskin with rubb until they sealed and repaired it, so its smell became good and the ghee was prevented from seeping, without spoiling its taste or smell. If they did not do this to the waterskin, the ghee would spoil. Adīm marbūb: a well-treated hide repaired with rubb. He says: They did the deed of this foolish woman, and what they strove to arrange and make was spoiled.]]

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bazīʿ told us, saying: Abū Maḥṣan narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: he said, "The sāhira is the earth. Have you not heard: 'For them is the game of the sea and the game of the sāhira'?"

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: "means the earth."

* Yaʿqūb told me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, saying: ʿUmāra ibn Abī Ḥafṣa narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: he said, "Then they will be on the face of the earth." He said: "Or have you not heard what Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt said to them:

'And in it is the flesh of the sāhira and the sea...'"

* ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: ʿUmāra narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: he said, "Then they will be on the face of the earth." Umayya said:

"And in it is the flesh of the sāhira and the sea..."

* Yaʿqūb told us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "Then they will be on the face of the earth."

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿with the sāhira﴾: he said, "The level place."

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: When the Resurrection seemed far away in the eyes of the people, God said: ﴿But it will be only a single blast, and at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾. He means: then they will be at the top of the earth after they had been in its belly.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿with the sāhira﴾: he said, "Then they will come out of their graves onto the surface of the earth. And the earth, the sāhira": he said, "Then they will come out."

* Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Khuṣayf, from ʿIkrima and Abū al-Haytham, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: he said, "On the earth."

* Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū al-Haytham, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, the same.

* Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿIkrima, the same.

* I was told by al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "The face of the earth."

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "The sāhira is the surface of the earth, above its back."

Others said: al-Sāhira is the name of a specific known place on the earth.

Those who said this:

* ʿAlī ibn Sahl told me, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to me, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀtika, regarding His words ﴿But it will be only a single blast, and at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "In the open land between the mountain of Ḥassān and the mountain of Arīḥā, which God extends however He wills."

* Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "A land in al-Shām."

Others said: It is a specific known mountain.

Those who said this:

* ʿAlī ibn Sahl told us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Bilāl narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, saying: Abū Sinān informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said regarding the words of God ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "The sāhira is a mountain beside Bayt al-Maqdis."

Others said: It is Jahannam.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Marwān al-ʿUqaylī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba narrated to me, from Qatada, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "In Jahannam."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verses 10–14:

On the explanation (ta'wil, interpretation) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Shall we indeed be returned to our former state? (10) Even when we have become decayed bones?" (11) They say, "That would then be a losing return." (12) But it will be only a single blast, (13) and at once they will be upon the awakened surface.﴾ (14)

Exalted is His remembrance. He says: These deniers of the Resurrection among the polytheists of Quraysh say, when they are told, "You will be resurrected after death": "Shall we indeed be returned to our former state before death, and come back alive as we were before our destruction and before our dying?" This is from their saying, "So-and-so returned upon his hafira (trail, the way he came)," meaning he went back the way he had come. From it is the words of the poet:

"Going back along our trail, over baldness and gray hair? God forbid such folly and frivolity."[[See what has passed above at hadith no. 151.]]

Those who explain the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* ʿAlī told me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿al-ḥāfira﴾: he said, "Life."

* Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾: he said, "Shall we indeed be made to live after our death and be resurrected from this place of ours?"

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?﴾ "Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿in the hāfira﴾: he said, "That is, shall we be returned as a new creation?"

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿That would then be a losing return﴾: "And what return is more losing than it? They were brought to life and then went to the Fire, so it was an evil return."

* * *

As for His words ﴿But it will be only a single blast﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: It will only be a single cry and one blast blown into the Trumpet, and that is the zajra (blast).

According to what we have said, the exegetes have said likewise.

* Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, and al-Ḥārith told me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His words ﴿a single blast﴾: he said, "A cry."

* Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿a single blast﴾: "The zajra is the blast in the Trumpet."

* * *

As for His words ﴿and at once they will be upon the awakened surface﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then at once these deniers of the Resurrection, who marvel at God's bringing them to life after their death, in denial of that, will be upon the sāhira (awakened surface), meaning the surface of the earth. The Arabs call the desert and the face of the earth sāhira, and I think they named it so because in it the animals sleep and stay awake, so it is described by a quality of what is in it. From it is the words of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:

"And in it is the flesh of the sāhira and the sea, and what they say is established for them."[[His Dīwān, poem 15/32. The lord of Kinda is Ḥujr, father of Imru' al-Qays. The lord of Maʿadd: Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr, as the commentator of his Dīwān says, though I am doubtful about it, for Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr was killed at al-Habāʾa. Labīd mentions Khabt and ʿAraʿar, which are two other places.]]

From it is also the words of Akhū Nahm on the day of Dhū Qār, to his horse:

"Advance, Miḥāj, for these are the bracelets (of the battle); and let no single unknown man terrify you. For your end is the dust of the sāhira, then you will return after it to the trail, after you were decayed bones."[[His Dīwān: 89; al-Mukhaṣṣaṣ 7:154. al-Ṭarīf and al-Ṭārif: newly acquired wealth, as opposed to al-Talīd and al-Tālid, which is the old wealth you were born with.]]

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said the same as what we have said.

* Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyān, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "A land in al-Shām."

Others said: It is a specific known mountain.

Those who said this:

* ʿAlī ibn Sahl told us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn Bilāl narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, saying: Abū Sinān informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said regarding the words of God ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "The sāhira is a mountain beside Bayt al-Maqdis."

Others said: It is Jahannam.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Marwān al-ʿUqaylī narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūba narrated to me, from Qatada, regarding ﴿at once they will be upon the sāhira﴾: "In Jahannam."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 15:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Has there reached you the account of Moses?﴾ (15)

.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 16–18:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa (16), "Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed (17), and say, 'Would you like to purify yourself (18)?'"﴾

Says Almighty God to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Has there come to you, O Muhammad, the report of Musa son of Imran, and have you heard his news when his Lord spoke to him in the sacred valley, meaning by 'sacred' the purified and blessed one? We have already mentioned the opinions of the scholars on this matter earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here. Likewise we have explained the meaning of His saying ﴿Tuwa﴾ and what the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) have said about it, but we will mention some of that here."

The interpreters differed regarding His saying ﴿Tuwa﴾. Some said: it is the name of the valley.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Tuwa﴾: it is the name of the valley.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa﴾: He said: the name of the sacred one is Tuwa.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley, Tuwa﴾: "We used to narrate that it was sanctified twice, and the name of the valley is Tuwa."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: tread the earth barefoot.

Some of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa﴾: He said: "Tread the earth with your foot."

Others said: rather, the meaning is that the valley was sanctified twice (tuwa meaning twice). We have explained all of that and its aspects earlier, sufficiently so that there is no need to repeat it here. Al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the ta', and said: blessing and sanctification were placed in it twice. Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated this to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan.

The readers differed in reciting it. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited ﴿Tuwa﴾ with a damma and without tanwin, while some readers of Syria and Kufa recited ﴿Tuwa﴾ with a damma on the ta' and with tanwin.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed﴾

Says Almighty God: Musa called to his Lord, [who said]: "Go to Pharaoh." The particle "an" (that) was omitted because the calling was a speech, so it is as if it were said to Musa: "His Lord said: Go to Pharaoh."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿For he has transgressed﴾

He says: he rebelled, exceeded his limit in aggression, and was arrogant toward his Lord.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then say, "Would you like to purify yourself?"﴾

He says: say to him: "Would you like to purify yourself from the defilement of disbelief and believe in your Lord?"

As narrated:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿Would you like to purify yourself?﴾: "To submit (tuslima)." He said: "Tazakka in the whole Qur'an means Islam," and he recited the saying of God: ﴿And that is the reward of one who purifies himself (tazakka)﴾, and he said: "one who embraced Islam." He recited ﴿And what would make you know that perhaps he would purify himself (yazzakka)?﴾ and said: "that he would submit." He recited ﴿And it would not be upon you that he does not purify himself (yazzakka)﴾, meaning: that he does not submit.

- Sa'id ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, regarding Musa's saying to Pharaoh: ﴿Would you like to purify yourself?﴾: "Would you like to say: There is no god but Allah."

The readers differed in reciting His saying ﴿tazakka﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina recited ﴿yazzakka﴾ with a doubled zay, while the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra recited ﴿tazakka﴾ with a single zay. Abu Amr used to say, as is reported from him, ﴿tazzakka﴾ with a doubled zay, meaning: "you give alms (tatasaddaqa) with zakat," so one would say "tatazakka," then it is assimilated. But Musa did not call Pharaoh to give alms while he was a disbeliever; he called him to Islam, so he said: "tazakka," meaning: that you become pure and a believer. The single zay is the more eloquent of the two readings in Arabic.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verses 19–24:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And I will guide you to your Lord, so that you may fear [Him]. Then he showed him the greatest sign. But he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned away, striving. And he gathered [his people] and proclaimed, saying, "I am your lord, the Most High."﴾

Says God, the Exalted, to His prophet Musa: "Say to Pharaoh: 'Is there for you a way to be guided to what pleases your Lord, which is the upright religion,' ﴿so that you may fear﴾, meaning: so that you may fear His punishment by performing what He has obligated upon you of His duties and avoiding what He has forbidden you of His sins."

* *

His saying: ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign﴾

Says God, the Exalted: Then Musa showed Pharaoh the greatest sign, meaning the greatest proof, that he was a messenger of God sent to him. That sign was Musa's hand when he brought it out white for the onlookers, and his staff when it turned into a clearly visible serpent.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Abu Za'ida Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sayf Abu Raja' — thus it is in my book, and I think it is from Nuh ibn Qays, from Muhammad ibn Sayf — who said: I heard al-Hasan say concerning this verse, ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign﴾: "His hand and his staff."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿the greatest sign﴾: "His staff and his hand."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign﴾: "He saw Musa's hand and his staff, and they were two signs."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, ﴿the greatest sign﴾: "His staff and his hand."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign﴾: "The staff and the serpent."
