He constructed it﴾ [79:27] ﴿He raised its ceiling and proportioned it﴾ [79:28]

Allah, may He be exalted in remembrance, means by His words ﴿So Allah seized him﴾: so Allah punished him ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾, meaning: the punishment of the Hereafter arising from his two utterances, which are His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ [79:24], and the first being His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ [28:38].

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Bakr, when he was asked about this, say: There were forty years between his words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and his words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. He said: They are his two utterances. ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾. It was said to him: Who transmitted this from you? He said: Abu Husayn. It was said to him: From Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas? He said: Yes.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: As for the first, it was when he said ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾, and as for the Hereafter, it was when he said ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Wadda' narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: It is His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. And there were forty years between them.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Asadi, from al-Sha'bi, similarly.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Amir, regarding ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: They are his two utterances, ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: So that is His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾, and the Hereafter is in His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, saying: Someone who heard Mujahid say informed me: There were forty years between the words of Pharaoh ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and his words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: As for the first, it was when Pharaoh said ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾, and as for the Hereafter, it was when he said ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. So Allah seized him with both his utterances, and drowned him in the sea.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: They differed about it. Some of them said: the punishment of the Hereafter is from his two utterances, and the first is His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

Others said: It is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter; Allah hastened for him the drowning, along with the punishment prepared for him in the Hereafter.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama al-Ju'fi, who said: There were forty years between the two utterances of Pharaoh: His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ and His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Thuwayr, from Mujahid, who said: Pharaoh remained among his people after he said ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ for forty years.

Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is: So Allah seized him with the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: the world and the Hereafter.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: the punishment of this world and the Hereafter; and this is also the view of Qatada.

Others said: The first is his disobedience to his Lord and his disbelief in Him, and the Hereafter is His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, saying: Someone who heard Mujahid say informed me: There were forty years between the words of Pharaoh ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and his words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: As for the first, it was when Pharaoh said ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾, and as for the Hereafter, it was when he said ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. So Allah seized him with both his utterances, and drowned him in the sea.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: They differed about it. Some of them said: the punishment of the Hereafter is from his two utterances, and the first is His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾ and His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

Others said: It is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter; Allah hastened for him the drowning, along with the punishment prepared for him in the Hereafter.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Khaythama al-Ju'fi, who said: There were forty years between the two utterances of Pharaoh: His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ and His words ﴿I know of no god for you other than me﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Thuwayr, from Mujahid, who said: Pharaoh remained among his people after he said ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ for forty years.

Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is: So Allah seized him with the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: the world and the Hereafter.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: the punishment of this world and the Hereafter; and this is also the view of Qatada.

Others said: The first is his disobedience to his Lord and his disbelief in Him, and the Hereafter is His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: The first is his denial and disobedience, and the Hereafter is His words ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. Then he recited: ﴿But he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned away, striving. And he gathered [his people] and called out. And said, "I am your lord, the most high."﴾ [79:21–24]. So that is the last utterance.

Others said: Rather, what is meant by it is that He seized him for his first deed and his last.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: his first deed and his last.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: his first deeds and his last.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Kalbi: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: the punishment of the Hereafter for the disobedience, and the first.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿as an example for the Hereafter and the first﴾: his deed for the Hereafter and the first.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, in that is a lesson for whoever fears [Allah]﴾:

Allah, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: Indeed, in the punishment with which Allah punished Pharaoh in the immediate world, and in His seizing him as an example for the Hereafter and the first, is an admonition and a lesson for whoever fears Allah and dreads His punishment. He made "an example for the Hereafter" a verbal noun (maṣdar) from His words ﴿So Allah seized him﴾, because His words ﴿So Allah seized him﴾ imply a punishment, so He made ﴿an example for the Hereafter﴾ a maṣdar from its meaning, not from its wording.

* *

As for His words ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He constructed it﴾:

Allah, may He be exalted in remembrance, says to the deniers of resurrection from Quraysh, who said ﴿When we are bones and decayed, [will we then be restored]? They say, "That, then, would be a losing return"﴾ [79:11–12]: Are you, O people, more difficult to create, or the heaven which your Lord built? For He who built the heaven and raised it as a ceiling finds your creation and the creation of your likes easy, and your being brought back to life after your death; and your creation after your death is not more difficult than the creation of the heaven. By His words ﴿He constructed it﴾ is meant: He raised it and made it a ceiling for the earth.

* *

As for His words ﴿He raised its ceiling and proportioned it﴾:

Allah, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: He proportioned the heaven, so that no part of it is higher than another, nor lower than another, but all of it is level in height and extent.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿He raised its ceiling and proportioned it﴾: he says: He raised its structure and proportioned it.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿He raised its ceiling﴾: He raised its structure without pillars.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿He raised its ceiling﴾: he says: its building.

* *

On His words, ﴿and He darkened its night﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He made the night of the sky dark. He attributed the night to the sky because the night is the setting of the sun, and its setting and rising occur in the sky, so it is attributed to it because it is in it, just as it is said "the stars of the night," since rising and setting occur in it.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said the same as what we have said about this.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and He darkened its night﴾, he said: "He made its night dark."

* * 

On His words, ﴿and brought forth its forenoon﴾:

He says: "and He brought forth its light," meaning: He manifested its daytime and made it clear, and illuminated its forenoon.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, (and brought forth its forenoon), he said: "The light of the day."

* * 

On His words, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿after that﴾. Some of them said: the earth was spread out after the creation of the heavens.

Those who said this:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words, where He mentions the creation of the earth before the heaven, then mentions the heaven before the earth. That is because God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it out before the heaven. Then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens. Then He spread out the earth after that, and that is His words: ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out, brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He anchored﴾, he said: He means that God created the heavens and the earth. When He finished with the heavens, before He created the sustenance of the earth in it, after the creation of the heaven, He anchored the mountains. By this he means the spreading out (dahw) of the sustenance, and the earth's sustenance and its plants could not be suitable except by the night and the day. That is His words: ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾. Did you not hear Him say: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾?

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Hafs, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The House was placed on the water on four pillars two thousand years before God created the world, and then the earth was spread out from beneath the House."

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: "God created the House two thousand years before the earth, and from it the earth was spread out."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "and the earth along with that He spread out." They said: The earth was created and spread out before the heaven, because God said: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾. They said: So God informed that He made the heavens after He had created all that is on the earth. They said: If that is so, then there is no sense to His words ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾ except what we have mentioned, that it means "along with that He spread it out." They said: This is like the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿Violent, after that, ignoble﴾, meaning: "along with that, ignoble." And as one says to a man: "You are a fool, and you are after this base of lineage," meaning: "along with this." And as His praised name said: ﴿And We had written in the Psalms after the Reminder﴾, meaning: "before the Reminder." And they cited the verse of al-Hudhali:

I praised my God after Urwa, when Khirash was saved,
and some evils are less harmful than others.[[His diwan: 29. It occurs in the commentary on the verse of Surah Al Imran: 79 (3: 233, Bulaq edition), and al-Mukhassas 17: 154. The poet says it to al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani, king of Ghassan, who is al-Harith al-A'raj, well known. Ibn Sida said: "Rububa: the plural of rabb, meaning the kings who were before you wasted my affair, and now my rububa (guardianship) has come to you, that is, the management and setting right of my affair. So rabb here means master, as if he said: those who used to rule my affair before you wasted it." Al-Tabari said later: "He means by his words 'rabbatī' (my guardianship): the one in charge of my affair and attending to it before you, who would nurture and set it right, but they did not set it right, and they wasted me, so I was lost." Al-Rababa: the kingdom, and it is also the covenant and pact. And with it this verse was interpreted, and they supported it with a narration that reads "amanati" (my trust) instead of "rababati." The first is better.]]

They claimed that Khirash was saved before Urwa.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from Mujahid, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, that he said: "And the earth at that He spread out."

* Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, he said: Ali ibn Ma'bad related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Salama related to us, from Khasif, from Mujahid, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

* Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, he said: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, from Abu Hamza, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

The view we mentioned from Ibn Abbas, that God created the earth and decreed its sustenance in it, and did not spread it out, then turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens, then spread out the earth after that, bringing forth from it its water and its pasture, and anchoring its mountains, is more in accord with what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates. This is because He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, and the known meaning of "after" (ba'da) is the opposite of the meaning of "before" (qabl). Nothing in God's spreading out the earth after His leveling the seven heavens, His darkening its night, and His bringing forth its forenoon requires that the earth was created after the creation of the heavens. This is because spreading out (al-dahw) in the speech of the Arabs means extension, and it is said from it: "dahā yadhū dahwan" and "dahaytu adhī dahyan," two dialects. And from it is the words of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt:

A house that He spread out, then He made us dwell in it,
and He settled the other, which is more glorious.[[In the printed edition: "from the kings who were", changed by them to match the phrasing they were accustomed to.]]

And the words of Aws ibn Hajar describing a rain cloud:

It shakes the pebbles from the fresh earth, kneeling down,
as if it were a sprinter or a playing, spreading one.[[Hadith 155: The discussion of the weakness of this isnad was previously given in detail, under number 137. This hadith is in Ibn Kathir 1: 44, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 13, and al-Shawkani 1: 11. The last two also attribute it to Ibn Abi Hatim. In the printed edition and Ibn Kathir: "and the earth and whatever is in them."]]

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾: that is, He spread it out.

* Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, he said: Rawwad related to us, from Abu Hamza, from al-Suddi, ﴿spread it out﴾, he said: "He spread it."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us: ﴿spread it out﴾, "He spread it."

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿spread it out﴾, he said: "He plowed it, split it," and said: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾, and he recited: ﴿Then We split the earth, splitting﴾, until He reached ﴿and fruit and grass﴾, and said: when He split it, He caused this to grow from it. And he recited: ﴿By the earth that splits open﴾.

* * 

On His words, ﴿He brought forth from it its water﴾:

He says: "He caused rivers to gush forth in it," ﴿and its pasture﴾, He says: "He caused its vegetation to grow."

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* I was told about al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words, ﴿and its pasture﴾: what God created in it of plants, and ﴿its water﴾: what He caused to gush forth in it of rivers.

* * 

On His words, ﴿and the mountains He anchored﴾:

He says: "and the mountains He set firmly in it," and there is an omitted element in the speech that is dispensed with by the indication of the speech of it, which is "in it," because the meaning of the speech is: "and the mountains He anchored in it."

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿and the mountains He anchored﴾, that is: He set them firmly so they do not shake their people.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Ata, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: "When God created the earth it trembled and said: 'You will create upon me Adam and his offspring, who will drop their filth upon me and commit sins upon me.' So God anchored it, and some of it is what you see and some is what you do not see. The first settling of the earth was like the flesh of a slaughtered camel, when its meat quivers after being slaughtered."

Ibn Sida said: "Rububa: the plural of rabb, meaning the kings who were before you wasted my affair, and now my rububa (guardianship) has come to you, that is, the management and setting right of my affair. So rabb here means master, as if he said: those who used to rule my affair before you wasted it." Al-Tabari said later: "He means by his words 'rabbatī' (my guardianship): the one in charge of my affair and attending to it before you, who would nurture and set it right, but they did not set it right, and they wasted me, so I was lost." Al-Rababa: the kingdom, and it is also the covenant and pact. And with it this verse was interpreted, and they supported it with a narration that reads "amanati" (my trust) instead of "rababati." The first is better.]]

They claimed that Khirash was saved before Urwa.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from Mujahid, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, that he said: "And the earth at that He spread out."

* Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, he said: Ali ibn Ma'bad related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Salama related to us, from Khasif, from Mujahid, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

* Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, he said: Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, from Abu Hamza, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, he said: "Along with that He spread it out."

The view we mentioned from Ibn Abbas, that God created the earth and decreed its sustenance in it, and did not spread it out, then turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens, then spread out the earth after that, bringing forth from it its water and its pasture, and anchoring its mountains, is more in accord with what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates. This is because He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾, and the known meaning of "after" (ba'da) is the opposite of the meaning of "before" (qabl). Nothing in God's spreading out the earth after His leveling the seven heavens, His darkening its night, and His bringing forth its forenoon requires that the earth was created after the creation of the heavens. This is because spreading out (al-dahw) in the speech of the Arabs means extension, and it is said from it: "dahā yadhū dahwan" and "dahaytu adhī dahyan," two dialects. And from it is the words of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt:

A house that He spread out, then He made us dwell in it,
and He settled the other, which is more glorious.[[In the printed edition: "from the kings who were", changed by them to match the phrasing they were accustomed to.]]

And the words of Aws ibn Hajar describing a rain cloud:

It shakes the pebbles from the fresh earth, kneeling down,
as if it were a sprinter or a playing, spreading one.[[Hadith 155: The discussion of the weakness of this isnad was previously given in detail, under number 137. This hadith is in Ibn Kathir 1: 44, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 13, and al-Shawkani 1: 11. The last two also attribute it to Ibn Abi Hatim. In the printed edition and Ibn Kathir: "and the earth and whatever is in them."]]

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿and the earth after that He spread out﴾: that is, He spread it out.

* Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, he said: Rawwad related to us, from Abu Hamza, from al-Suddi, ﴿spread it out﴾, he said: "He spread it."

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us: ﴿spread it out﴾, "He spread it."

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿spread it out﴾, he said: "He plowed it, split it," and said: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾, and he recited: ﴿Then We split the earth, splitting﴾, until He reached ﴿and fruit and grass﴾, and said: when He split it, He caused this to grow from it. And he recited: ﴿By the earth that splits open﴾.

* * 

On His words, ﴿He brought forth from it its water﴾:

He says: "He caused rivers to gush forth in it," ﴿and its pasture﴾, He says: "He caused its vegetation to grow."

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

* I was told about al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words, ﴿and its pasture﴾: what God created in it of plants, and ﴿its water﴾: what He caused to gush forth in it of rivers.

* * 

On His words, ﴿and the mountains He anchored﴾:

He says: "and the mountains He set firmly in it," and there is an omitted element in the speech that is dispensed with by the indication of the speech of it, which is "in it," because the meaning of the speech is: "and the mountains He anchored in it."

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, ﴿and the mountains He anchored﴾, that is: He set them firmly so they do not shake their people.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Ata, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali, who said: "When God created the earth it trembled and said: 'You will create upon me Adam and his offspring, who will drop their filth upon me and commit sins upon me.' So God anchored it, and some of it is what you see and some is what you do not see. The first settling of the earth was like the flesh of a slaughtered camel, when its meat quivers after being slaughtered."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 33–36:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿A provision for you and your livestock﴾ (33) ﴿So when the Great Calamity comes﴾ (34) ﴿On the Day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ (35) ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever sees﴾ (36)

He, may He be exalted and remembered, means by His words ﴿A provision for you and your livestock﴾ that He created these things and brought forth from the earth its water and its pasture as a benefit for us and a provision for a time.

* *

As for His words ﴿So when the Great Calamity comes﴾:

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: So when there comes that which overwhelms every dreadful matter, engulfing everything else with its great terror. It has also been said that it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So when the Great Calamity comes﴾: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants of.

* Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, he said: Sahl ibn Amir narrated to us, he said: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, regarding His words ﴿So when the Great Calamity comes﴾, he said: the people of Paradise will be driven to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

* *

As for His words ﴿On the Day when man will remember what he strove for﴾:

He says: when the Calamity comes, on the Day when man will remember what he did in the world of good and evil, and that is his striving. ﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth﴾ means: the Fire will be made manifest, and it is the Fire of Allah, for whoever sees it, meaning for the eyes of those who look.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 37–46:

The interpretation of the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿But as for he who transgressed (37) And preferred the worldly life (38) Then indeed Hellfire will be his refuge (39) But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [its] desire (40) Then indeed Paradise will be his refuge (41)﴾

.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for he who rebelled against his Lord, disobeyed Him, and was arrogant toward worshipping Him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿taghā﴾ [transgressed]: He said: "disobeyed."

* *

His words: ﴿And preferred the worldly life﴾

He says: And he preferred the enjoyment of the worldly life over the honor of the Hereafter and what God has prepared therein for His friends. So he worked for the world, strove for it, and abandoned working for the Hereafter. ﴿Then indeed Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ He says: Then indeed the Fire of God, which is named al-Jahim, is his abode and his shelter, and his destination to which he will go on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

And His words: ﴿But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [its] desire﴾

He says: And as for he who feared God's questioning him when he stands before Him on the Day of Resurrection, and so he guarded himself against Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. ﴿And prevented the soul from [its] desire﴾ He says: And he restrained his soul from its desire in what God dislikes and does not approve of from it, so he restrained it from that and opposed its desire in favor of what his Lord commanded him. ﴿Then indeed Paradise will be his refuge﴾ He says: Then indeed Paradise is his shelter and his abode on the Day of Resurrection.

We have already mentioned the statements of the people of interpretation concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿And for he who fears the position of his Lord﴾ earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

* *

The interpretation of the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? (42) About what are you [concerned] to mention it? (43) To your Lord is its finality (44) You are only a warner for those who fear it (45) As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained [in the world] except for an evening or its morning (46)﴾

.

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: These deniers of the Resurrection ask you, O Muhammad, about the Hour in which the dead will be raised from their graves. ﴿When is its arrival﴾, meaning: when will it stand and appear? Al-Farra' used to say: If someone says: "Irsa" (anchoring) is for the ship, the mountains that are firmly set, and similar things, then how is the Hour described with irsa? I say: It is like a ship when it is moving and then anchors, and its anchoring is its standing up. He said: Its standing is not like the standing of one who stands; it is only like your saying: "Justice has stood" and "the truth has stood," meaning it appeared and was established.

Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him, says: God says to His Prophet: ﴿About what are you [concerned] to mention it﴾, meaning: About what matter are you in mentioning the Hour and inquiring into its affair? It is mentioned that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to frequently mention the Hour, until this verse was revealed.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from A'isha, who said: The Prophet ﷺ did not cease asking about the Hour until God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿About what are you [concerned] to mention it, to your Lord is its finality﴾.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isma'il, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: The Prophet ﷺ would not cease mentioning the matter of the Hour until ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival ...﴾ to ﴿who fears it﴾ was revealed.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿About what are you [concerned] to mention it﴾: He said: "the Hour."

* *

His words: ﴿To your Lord is its finality﴾

He says: To your Lord is the end of its knowledge; that is, knowledge of the Hour ends with Him, and none other knows the time of its standing.

* *

His words: ﴿You are only a warner for those who fear it﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Muhammad: You are only a messenger sent to warn of the Hour those who fear God's punishment therein for their crimes, and you were not charged with knowing the time of its standing. He says: So leave what you were not charged to know, and act upon what you were commanded, namely warning those you were commanded to warn.

The reciters differed in the reading of His words ﴿mundhiru man yakhshaha﴾. Abu Ja'far the reciter and Ibn Muhaysin used to read ﴿mundhirun﴾ with tanwin, meaning: he is a warner of those who fear it. The rest of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, Kufa, and Basra read ﴿mundhiru﴾ with idafa to ﴿man﴾.

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that these are two well-known readings, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

* *

His words: ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained [in the world] except for an evening or its morning﴾

May His praise be exalted, says: As if these deniers of the Hour, on the day they see that the Hour has arisen, because of its tremendous terror, had not remained in the world except for an evening of a day, or the morning of that evening. The Arabs say: "I will come to you in the evening or its morning," and "I will come to you in the morning or its evening," so they use the meaning of ghadah (morning) as the beginning of the day and ashiyyah (evening) as the end of the day. Likewise His words ﴿except for an evening or its morning﴾ mean only the end of a day or its beginning. And they recite this verse:

"We attacked 'Amir in their abode, at the evening of the crescent or its nightfall"

meaning: the evening of the crescent, or the evening of the sirar (the last night of the lunar month).

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained [in the world] except for an evening or its morning﴾: the time of the world in the eyes of the people when they witness the Hereafter.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Nazi'at.
